name: Solitaire
intro: Learn Klondike Solitaire step by step: the layout, building down the columns, the deck and foundations, then the strategy that wins more games: uncovering cards, Kings and empty columns, and using the deck.

units.name: How Solitaire works
units.blurb: The layout, building, the deck and empty columns.

lessons.title: How to play Klondike Solitaire: the setup
lessons.summary: Klondike Solitaire in two minutes: the seven columns, the deck, the four foundations and the goal of building each suit from Ace to King.
lessons.wrap: Seven columns, a deck and four foundations. Next: building down the columns.

position.stock: QH 6C JH JS 5C 6D QC 3C 7S 4D 10D 10H 2C 9D QS 4S JC 8D 9S 2H 5S 2D 7C KD

steps.text: Solitaire (Klondike) is dealt into seven columns. The first has one card, the last has seven, and only the bottom card of each is face up. The rest of the deck goes face down in the deck at the top left.

position.stock: QH 6C JH JS 5C 6D QC 3C 7S 4D 10D 10H 2C 9D QS 4S JC 8D 9S 2H 5S 2D 7C KD

steps.text: The four empty spaces at the top right are the foundations. The goal is to move every card there, one pile per suit, in order from Ace up to King.
steps.wrong: The foundations are the four spaces at the top right, marked with suits.
steps.done: Each foundation holds one suit, Ace first.

position.stock: QH 6C JH JS 5C 6D QC 3C 7S 4D 10D 10H 2C 9D QS 4S JC 8D 9S 2H 5S 2D 7C KD

steps.text: Aces always start a foundation. Tap a card, then tap where it should go.
steps.prompt: Move an Ace up to the foundations.
steps.wrong: Find an Ace among the face-up cards.
steps.done: The first card home. 51 to go.

lessons.title: Solitaire rules: building down the columns
lessons.summary: In Solitaire, cards stack down the columns in alternating colours: a red 8 on a black 9. Learn to build and to move whole runs of cards.
lessons.wrap: Down by one, alternating colours, and runs move together. Next: the deck and empty columns.

steps.text: In the columns, you build downwards in alternating colours: a card can go on one that is one higher and the other colour. A red 8 goes on a black 9.
steps.prompt: Put the 8 of hearts on the 9 of clubs.
steps.wrong: Tap the 8 of hearts, then the 9 of clubs.

steps.text: A run of cards in order can move together. Tap the top card of the run to pick up the whole run.
steps.prompt: Move the 9 of clubs, with the 8 of hearts on it, onto the 10 of diamonds.
steps.wrong: Tap the 9 of clubs (not the 8), then the 10 of diamonds.
steps.done: The whole run moved, and the 10 of diamonds is still the base.

steps.text: Quick check.
steps.prompt: Can the 7 of hearts go on the 8 of diamonds?
steps.explain: No. Columns must alternate colours: a red 7 needs a black 8.

lessons.title: Solitaire rules: the deck and empty columns
lessons.summary: How the Solitaire deck works, how cards climb the foundations in order, and why only a King can fill an empty column.
lessons.wrap: Draw when you’re stuck, build the foundations in order, and only Kings fill gaps. Next: a quick rules check.

steps.text:
When you need more cards, tap the deck to turn one over onto the waste pile next to it. The top card of the waste can be played.

When the deck runs out, tap its empty space to turn the waste back over and go through it again.
steps.prompt: Draw a card from the deck.
steps.wrong: Tap the face-down deck at the top left.

steps.text: That Ace can go straight up.
steps.prompt: Move the Ace of clubs to the foundations.
steps.wrong: Tap the Ace on the waste pile, then a foundation.
steps.done: Now the 2 of clubs can follow it.

steps.text: Foundations build up in order and in suit: Ace, 2, 3, and so on.
steps.prompt: Move the 2 of clubs onto the Ace of clubs.
steps.wrong: Tap the 2 of clubs at the bottom of the last column, then the clubs foundation.
steps.done: And a face-down card turned over underneath.

steps.text: An empty column can only be filled with a King, along with any run on it.
steps.prompt: Move a King into the empty column.
steps.wrong: Only a King can go into an empty column.
steps.done: The King moves over and the card under it turns face up.

units.blurb: Show you know the rules, then on to strategy.

lessons.title: Solitaire rules check
lessons.summary: A quick Solitaire rules check: play an Ace up, build a column and answer a question. Pass it to unlock the strategy lessons.
lessons.wrap: Rules done. Now for the strategy that wins more games.

steps.prompt: Build the 8 of hearts onto a column.

steps.text: Last one.

options: Only a King, or a run starting with a King
steps.explain: Only a King, with any cards stacked on it.

units.name: Winning ideas
units.blurb: Uncovering cards, Kings, foundations and the deck.

lessons.title: Solitaire strategy: uncover the hidden cards
lessons.summary: The key to winning Klondike Solitaire: free the face-down cards, starting with the columns that hide the most. Learn to pick the right move.
lessons.wrap: When you have a choice, dig into the biggest pile of face-down cards. Next: empty columns and Kings.

steps.text:
Every game is won by turning over the face-down cards in the columns. Most of the cards you need are hidden there.

So when two moves look the same, choose the one that works on the column with the most face-down cards.
Both black 7s can go on the 8 of diamonds. The 7 of clubs sits alone. The 7 of spades has four face-down cards under it.
steps.prompt: Make the move that does the most good.
steps.wrong: That move doesn’t turn anything over. Move the other 7.
steps.done: A face-down card turns over, and that column is shorter now.

lessons.title: Solitaire strategy: empty columns and Kings
lessons.summary: An empty column in Solitaire is powerful but only a King can fill it. Learn when to empty a column and when to keep it for the right King.
lessons.wrap: Empty a column when a King is ready to use it. Next: when to play cards up to the foundations.

steps.text: An empty column is valuable: it’s the only way to move a King and free the cards under it.
steps.prompt: You can empty a column, but there’s no King ready to move into it. Is it worth it?
options: Only if it frees something useful; otherwise it may sit empty for a long time
steps.explain: An empty column only helps when you have a King to put there. Emptying one early can waste moves.

steps.text: Here a King is waiting on top of face-down cards.
steps.wrong: Move the King of hearts into the empty column to free the cards under it.
steps.done: The King moves over, and the Jack of diamonds under it turns face up.

lessons.title: Solitaire strategy: when to play cards up
lessons.summary: Should every card go up to the foundations straight away? In Solitaire, Aces and 2s always should, but higher cards are sometimes needed in the columns.
lessons.wrap: Aces and 2s go up at once; higher cards when they aren’t needed below. Next: using the deck well.

position.stock: QH 6C JH JS 5C 6D QC 3C 7S 4D 10D 10H 2C 9D QS 4S JC 8D 9S 2H 5S 2D 7C KD

steps.text:
Aces and 2s should always go up straight away: nothing can be built on them in the columns.

Higher cards are different. A black 6 on the foundation can no longer hold a red 5 in the columns. If the red 5s are still buried, you might need that 6 below.
Think about it.
steps.prompt: You can play the 6 of spades up, but both red 5s are still face down. What’s safest?
options: Leave it in the column for now, in case a red 5 needs a home
steps.explain: Keep it below until the red 5s are free or the 6 is in the way. A card on the foundation can’t hold anything in the columns.

lessons.title: Solitaire strategy: using the deck well
lessons.summary: Make the most of the Solitaire deck: play the columns first, draw only when stuck, and remember the cards you pass in the waste pile.
lessons.wrap: Columns first, deck second. That’s the Solitaire path complete!

position.stock: QH 6C JH JS 5C 6D QC 3C 7S 4D 10D 10H 2C 9D QS 4S JC 8D 9S 2H 5S 2D 7C KD

steps.text:
Cards in the deck aren’t going anywhere, but face-down column cards stay stuck until you free them. So make every useful column move first, then draw.

BoardGameSite lets you draw one card at a time or three. Draw 3 is harder: you can only play the top card of each three.
Check the idea.
steps.prompt: You have a column move and could also draw. Which first?
options: Draw first, to see more cards
steps.explain: Column moves can turn over hidden cards. Drawing can wait.

steps.text: Last question.
steps.explain: Draw 1: every card in the deck is playable as you go through it.
